basis: Limb malformations and abnormal nail placement define the syndrome; hydronephrosis and vesicoureteral reflux each reported in 1/3 patients.
Inherited variation in LDL molecular properties falls within lipid metabolism; no direct organ injury documented.
Complex spastic paraplegia; reduced visual acuity in 3/3 and optic disc pallor in 30-79% support ocular damage. Muscle wasting is neurogenic.
Disordered proximal tibial growth produces progressive skeletal deformity.
Mature teratoma arising in the central nervous system.
Spastic paraplegia, dementia and destructive optic atrophy are defining manifestations.
Coagulopathy with dermal microvascular thrombosis and hemorrhagic skin necrosis defines purpura fulminans; an infectious trigger is a separate condition.
Recessive skeletal-muscle titinopathy; cardiomyopathy is subtype-dependent and not established in at least 30% across this umbrella.
Skeletal dysplasia and dentinogenesis imperfecta define the disease; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 4/10. Renal disease in 1/10 is below threshold.
Benign adipocytic tumor predominantly arising in subcutaneous tissue; deeper locations do not establish common additional organ damage.
Possible steroid-metabolism defect causing persistent fever; mechanism uncertain. [Summary](https://mips.helmholtz-muenchen.de/phenodis/disease/show/9946)
Definition specifies cervical adenocarcinoma arising from mesonephric remnants; the renal carcinoma ancestry conflicts with its stated origin.
Glycogen branching-enzyme deficiency with severe prenatal myopathy and fetal akinesia; respiratory failure alone does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Mitochondrial heart/brain disease; myopathy defines the syndrome, with hypotonia in 1/1. Retinopathy in 1/1 omitted at the four-axis cap.
Astrocytic tumor arising in the central nervous system.
Squamous cell carcinoma originating in the urethra, which belongs to the renal axis.
Craniofacial/cervical bone disease and defining periodontal destruction. [Case report](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7811426/)
Congenital dermal hamartomatous tumor containing malformed hair follicles.
Severe intellectual developmental disorder with seizures, absent speech and central motor abnormalities; no established metabolic disease phenotype.
Central and peripheral motor dysfunction with developmental impairment; respiratory symptoms do not establish intrinsic lung damage, and infections are separate.
Congenital structural abnormality of the mitral valve supporting apparatus.
Zellweger metabolic disorder with defining brain/liver dysfunction; renal cystic disease reported in 1/1. Ocular and hearing involvement omitted at the four-axis cap.
Isolated neurologic dystonia; limb, tongue and laryngeal contractions do not establish separate muscle, gastrointestinal or airway damage.
Toxic injury with obliteration of bronchioles; no infectious or autoimmune mechanism is specified.
Disordered thirst and water balance; polyuria does not imply intrinsic renal damage, and structural hypothalamic injury is not universal.
